name: Dual On/Off Outlet
description: An in-wall duplex outlet with two receptacles that can each be switched on and off independently over Insteon. It is used to control plug-in lamps, fans, and small appliances.

steps.text: Turn off power to the outlet at the electrical service panel.
Remove the old outlet and disconnect the wires, leaving 1/2 in. (12 mm) of bare wire.
Turn on power at the circuit breaker.
Use a voltage detector to identify the line wire; line will be energized.
Turn off power at the circuit breaker.

Connect the outlet's wires to the line, neutral and ground wires in the junction box per the installation diagram for an end-of-run, middle-of-run or switched outlet. Verify that the wire nuts are secure and no copper is exposed.
Mount the outlet into the junction box.
Turn power on to the outlet at the circuit breaker panel.
Test the outlet by tapping one of the SET buttons to turn it on and off.
steps.expect: The outlet turns on and off

steps.text: Reattach the wall plate.

notes: Replacing a switched outlet requires removing the wall switch from the circuit; the switch can be replaced by an Insteon switch or keypad if control is still wanted.
The upper SET button controls the upper outlet and the lower SET button the lower outlet.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button of the outlet you want to link (upper or lower) until it beeps.
steps.expect: Status LED blinks green; the outlet stays in linking mode until a link is made

notes: The first device put into linking mode becomes the controller and the second becomes the responder.
Each outlet has its own SET button and links separately.
With the Hub, follow the app's instructions and press and hold one of the SET buttons when prompted.
Software can use the Enter Linking Mode command (On/Off Outlet Developer Notes).

verification.note: When adding the outlet to the Hub, the On/Off Outlet 2663-222 Owner's Manual says to hold a SET button until the outlet beeps; the On/Off Outlet 2663-222 Quick Start Guide says until it double-beeps. The catalog uses the owner's manual's single beep.

steps.text: Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the controller, for group 0.
Press and hold the SET button of the outlet you want to link (upper or lower) until it beeps.
steps.expect: Status LED blinks green; the outlet stays in linking mode until a link is made

steps.text: Wait for the Hub to report the new link.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send ID Request.
steps.expect: The device answers with its category, subcategory and firmware version

steps.text: Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1: as an extended message if Get Insteon Engine Version (cmd1 0x0D) says the device is i2CS, and as a standard message otherwise.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the responder.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send Ping to confirm the link.

notes: This links the Hub's group 0 to the device as a responder, and the device's group 1 to the Hub as a controller, so the Hub receives the device's reports.

To add the device without its SET button, have the Hub send it Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09, cmd2 0x01; extended for an i2CS device) right after it starts ALL-Linking, in place of the SET button step.

verification.note: Assembled from this profile's linking steps and the standard Insteon commands Start ALL-Linking, ID Request, Enter Linking Mode and Ping; no document describes adding this product to a Hub.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the outlet beeps.
Tap the SET button.
steps.expect: Status LED double-blinks green; multi-linking mode lasts four minutes or until the SET button is tapped

steps.text: Link each responder in turn: on most devices, press and hold its SET button.
Tap the SET button to exit.
Press and hold the SET button until the outlet beeps.
Press and hold the SET button again.
steps.expect: Status LED blinks red; the outlet stays in unlinking mode until a link is removed

notes: For multi-unlinking, tap the SET button after entering unlinking mode (Status LED double-blinks red); the outlet stays in multi-unlinking mode for four minutes or until the SET button is tapped.

steps.text: Press and hold the upper SET button for 3 seconds.
steps.expect: Outlet beeps and its status LED blinks green

steps.text: While the status LED blinks green, press and hold the upper SET button again for 3 seconds.
steps.expect: Outlet beeps and its status LED blinks red

steps.text: Quickly tap the upper SET button twice and wait for the beep.
Immediately press and hold the upper SET button until the long beep stops.
Release the upper SET button.
steps.expect: Outlet double-beeps and both the top and bottom status LEDs turn on green

notes: A soft factory reset erases all device settings, including links made with the top and bottom outlets.
The On/Off Outlet 2663-222 Owner's Manual's flow chart shows that tapping the SET button instead of holding it at the last step exits without resetting.
If the outlet does not respond, use the alternate procedure.

verification.note: The On/Off Outlet 2663-222 Owner's Manual gives the soft factory reset only as a flow chart labeled with the upper and lower SET buttons; the Factory Resetting Insteon Devices (Insteon support article) gives it in words for dual on/off wall outlets, using the top button, with the beeps and LED colors.

steps.text: Turn off power to the outlet at the electrical service panel.
Press and hold the upper SET button.
While you keep holding the SET button, have an assistant turn power back on at the service panel.
When the long beep ends, release the SET button.

notes: An assistant is needed to turn power off and on at the service panel while you hold the SET button.

steps.text: Remove the outlet's links from every controller that controls it, using the unlinking steps or software.

notes: The On/Off Outlet 2663-222 Owner's Manual's troubleshooting says that links to devices removed from the network must be removed from their controllers; otherwise the controllers keep repeating commands and slow the network.

verification.note: Taken from the On/Off Outlet 2663-222 Owner's Manual's troubleshooting section, not a removal procedure.

steps.text: Remove the device from its scenes first, so no other device keeps links to it.
Have the Hub send Enter Unlinking Mode (cmd1 0x0A) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1, as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF (delete), so the device deletes its group 1 link to the Hub.
steps.expect: The device deletes its group 1 link to the Hub, and the Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub start unlinking for group 0 (Start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF).
Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1, as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Wait for the Hub to report that the link is gone.
steps.expect: The Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

notes: Inferred: seen on three i2CS devices (Outdoor On/Off Plug 2634-222 firmware 0x42, On/Off Plug 2635-222 firmware 0x48, I/O Module 2450 firmware 0x41) linked to a Hub 2245, these steps should remove every link between the Hub and the device with no SET button press. First the device's group 1 link: Enter Unlinking Mode (cmd1 0x0A) is sent to the device while the modem joins as responder. Then the modem's group 0 link: the modem starts ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF while the device is sent Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09).

verification.note: Assembled from the standard Insteon commands Enter Unlinking Mode, Start ALL-Linking and Enter Linking Mode; no document describes removing this product from a Hub.

notes: Both outlets are switched, each by its own group.
An August 2014 owner's manual prints subcategory 0x29, the 2476ST's; the December 2014 manual gives 0x39.
sources: Factory Resetting Insteon Devices (Insteon support article)
